enriched_description: Sound transduction device with a cylindrical or spherical head containing a mesh grille covering the diaphragm element. The head is mounted on a cylindrical body or handle approximately 15-25 cm long. Mesh grille is made of fine steel wire woven into a hemispherical pattern with a metallic silver or black finish. Body is smooth metal or plastic with an on/off switch and volume control. XLR or 1/4-inch connector protrudes from the base. Some models have a shock mount suspension system. Surface shows a combination of polished metal grille and matte-finished body.

Countertop kitchen appliance with a rectangular box-shaped body and a front-opening door with a transparent window. The door has a dark-tinted glass panel framed by a plastic or metal border, with a handle on the right or left side. Control panel is located on the right side of the door, featuring a digital display and push-button or dial controls. Body dimensions approximately 45-55 cm wide by 30-35 cm tall by 35-45 cm deep. Exterior finish is white, black, or stainless steel with a smooth glossy or brushed surface. Interior cavity is visible through the window when illuminated.

Prescribed identifying garment for military personnel consisting of a structured jacket and matching trousers in olive drab, camouflage, or formal dress colors. The jacket has a stand collar or notched lapels, button-front closure, shoulder epaulets, and multiple patch pockets with flaps. Fabric is a durable cotton-polyester blend or wool with a matte textured surface. Camouflage patterns feature irregular splotches of green, brown, tan, and black. Rank insignia, name tapes, and unit patches are visible on the chest and shoulders. Trousers have a straight-leg cut with cargo pockets on the thighs.

Large cylindrical metal container for transporting milk, typically made of galvanized steel or aluminum with a tall narrow profile. Height approximately 60-90 cm with a diameter of 30-40 cm. The can has a slightly tapered body widening toward the base for stability. Top features a narrow neck with a wide flanged rim and a domed or flat lid. Two metal handles are attached to the sides near the top for carrying. Surface is polished or brushed metal with a silver-gray finish, showing horizontal seam lines from manufacturing. The base has a rolled edge for structural reinforcement.

Compact passenger bus designed to carry 4-10 passengers, with a boxy body shape shorter than a full-size bus. Features a front engine compartment, large windshield, and a row of side windows along the passenger area. Body length approximately 5-8 meters with a height of 2.5-3 meters. Entrance door is located at the front or mid-body, either sliding or folding. Exterior paint is typically white, yellow, or a company livery with route markings. Wheels are standard van-sized with steel or alloy rims. Rear has a flat or slightly angled panel with taillights and license plate mount.

Very short skirt with a hemline ending well above the knee, typically 10-25 cm below the waistband. Constructed from woven fabric (denim, cotton, polyester, or leather) with a smooth or textured surface. The skirt has a fitted waistband with a zipper or button closure at the front, side, or back. Silhouette ranges from A-line flaring outward to straight pencil-cut. Fabric drapes from the waist with minimal gathering or pleating. Surface may feature solid colors, patterns, or decorative elements like pockets, stitching, or embellishments. Leg exposure is significant due to the short hemline.

Small box-shaped passenger van with a tall roofline and sliding rear side doors for easy access to rear seating. Body profile is characterized by a short hood, large greenhouse (window area), and a nearly vertical rear hatch. Length approximately 4.5-5 meters with a height of 1.7-1.8 meters. Interior features multiple rows of seats (typically 2-3 rows) with removable or fold-flat capability. Exterior paint in family-oriented colors with chrome or body-colored trim. Front grille and headlights follow contemporary automotive styling. Rear liftgate opens upward to reveal cargo area behind the rearmost seats.

Cylindrical rocket-shaped weapon with a pointed nose cone, smooth metallic body, and stabilizing fins at the rear. The body is a long tube approximately 2-15 meters in length with a diameter of 20-60 cm. Nose cone is ogive or conical in shape, painted in military gray, green, or white. The midsection may have markings, serial numbers, or warning labels. Rear section features swept-back fins (typically 4) arranged symmetrically around the body for aerodynamic stability. Surface finish is smooth painted metal with visible panel lines and attachment points. Exhaust nozzle is visible at the extreme rear.

Hand covering glove with a separate compartment for the thumb and a single shared compartment for the remaining four fingers. Constructed from knitted wool, fleece, leather, or synthetic insulated material with a soft textured surface. The mitten has a rounded bulbous shape at the finger end due to the shared compartment. Cuff extends 5-15 cm up the wrist, often with ribbed elastic knit for a snug fit. Surface may feature cable-knit patterns, Fair Isle designs, or solid colors. Palm side may have reinforced grip material or suede patches. Thumb protrudes from the side at an angle.

Deep round bowl designed for use with an electric mixer, typically made of stainless steel, glass, or ceramic. The bowl has a wide circular opening tapering to a narrower base with smooth curved interior walls. Diameter at the rim ranges from 20-30 cm with a depth of 10-15 cm. Stainless steel bowls have a polished reflective interior and a brushed exterior surface. Glass bowls are transparent with a smooth glossy finish. Ceramic bowls have a glazed exterior with decorative colors or patterns. The base is flat and stable. Some bowls have a non-slip rubber ring on the bottom or a pouring spout on the rim.
